scope: 15 runtime sheets / 688 frame cells / 72 directional action sequences
status: art rejected; existing runtime preserved for review

clips.title: Idle
clips.issue: Mask changes expression: down frames 3–4 compress the eye markings and widen the mouth; right frames 3–4 look like a blink. Left face also shifts. Mask must be a rigid object.

clips.title: Run
clips.issue: DOWN: hands stay together at chest all 12 frames; sword reads as sheathed. LEFT: fixed raised hands all 12 frames. UP: both arms drop/spread together around frames 3–9. RIGHT: better leg stride, but exposed oval mask and missing fringe differ from idle. All four rows need correction.

clips.title: Start moving
clips.issue: All directions change hair/head/sword design by frame 3 to match the rejected run. Right and left frame 2 contain competing blade-like shapes. Fix after replacing run; these transitions cannot remain.

clips.title: Stop moving
clips.issue: Head/fringe and weapon jump from run design back to idle. Down frame 0 keeps clasped hands; left frame 0 keeps the folded-arm run. Replace alongside start/run.

clips.title: Turn
clips.issue: Mostly a small ready-pose foot shuffle; does not bridge the running pose. Lower priority than run, but match the replacement stance and locked mask.

clips.title: Dash
clips.issue: Right/left have readable forward lean. Down has compressed hop-like poses; up mostly pushes hair sideways. Keep as motion reference, review mask and joins before accepting.

clips.title: Crescent cast
clips.issue: Free hand extends and sword stays held. Down hand points sideways; up hand points sideways too. Check direction-specific cast silhouette. Up frame 4 has art touching a cell edge.

clips.title: Riposte guard
clips.issue: Guard idea is readable. Right rotates toward camera; left lifts sword alongside head. Keep two-handed grip here only where intentional; mask and recovery still need a consistency pass.

clips.title: Hit reaction
clips.issue: Right poses resemble a forward dash more than recoil. Down/left around frame 5 change the mouth into an open expression. North turns sword forward. Rework recoil and keep rigid mask.

clips.title: Charge preparation
clips.issue: Mask/hair design changes through preparation. Down final pose rotates to three-quarter; left late frames expose the smooth oval mask. Down frame 2 reaches a cell edge.

clips.title: Charged hold
clips.issue: Down sword oscillates from left to right within the hold loop; should mostly hold tension. Left frame 3 flares hair sharply. Mask and head differ from normal idle/run.

clips.title: Combo 1 — cut
clips.issue: Cut has windup/follow-through, but right turns frontward and left resembles an overhead cut. Keep direction-specific contact consistent. Up frame 6 touches a cell edge; standardize mask.

clips.title: Combo 2 — thrust
clips.issue: Right/left thrusts read clearly. Up contact extends sideways instead of strongly up; needs a clearer foreshortened thrust. Right recovery frame 5 touches a cell edge. Down mask changes during recovery.

clips.title: Combo 3 — rising cut
clips.issue: Rising sword path is visible, but direction rows have different body turns/kicks. Down frame 1 touches a cell edge. Review weapon continuity and locked mask before accepting.

clips.title: Combo 4 — finisher
clips.issue: Down/right show overhead-to-low contact; left has a much less decisive finish and jumps to ready sooner. Mask/head still change with pose. Keep distinct finisher silhouette in all directions.

clips.title: Charged release
clips.issue: Left contact turns almost frontward and down frames 9–10 open the mask mouth. Right release reads more like a thrust. Standardize the intended broad cleave and rigid mask.

clips.title: Slime to human
clips.issue: Reverse of transform-out. Directional morphs exist, but inherit changing human mask and unrelated facial expressions. Check mask becoming solid and the join to idle after canonical head is fixed.

clips.title: Human to slime
clips.issue: Down human frames 3–7 change facial markings before liquefying. Side morphs alter face/head during transition. The mask can dissolve with the body, but should not emote while still solid.
